name: Brandon Johnson
description: Brandon Johnson (born March 27, 1976, in Elgin, Illinois) is Chicago's 57th mayor, in office since May 15, 2023 (record current as of October 2026). A graduate of Aurora University, he began his career as a social studies teacher in Chicago Public Schools, at Jenner Academy in Cabrini-Green and at Westinghouse College Prep, then became an organizer with the Chicago Teachers Union, helping organize the union's 2012 strike. In 2018 he was elected Cook County commissioner for the 1st District, defeating the incumbent; he was re-elected in 2022. On the county board he led passage of the Just Housing Ordinance, which barred housing discrimination against formerly incarcerated people. Johnson advanced from the February 2023 first round and won the April 4, 2023 runoff against Paul Vallas, succeeding Lori Lightfoot. He lives in Chicago's Austin community.

name: Black Panther
description: Black Panther, directed by Ryan Coogler for Marvel Studios and distributed by Walt Disney Pictures, premiered on January 29, 2018, and opened in the United States that February 16, carrying the Marvel apparatus to Wakanda — an African nation imagined as never colonized, its technology and tradition fused — and to the argument between T'Challa's inheritance and Killmonger's indictment of it. It was the first superhero film nominated for the Academy Award for Best Picture and the first Marvel Cinematic Universe film to win an Oscar, taking three from seven nominations: costume design for Ruth Carter, production design for Hannah Beachler and Jay Hart, and original score for Ludwig Göransson. Carter and Beachler were the first Black winners in their Oscar categories. It grossed more than $1.3 billion worldwide, stood as 2018's highest-grossing film domestically, and at release was the highest-grossing film ever directed by a Black filmmaker. The graph files it as the blockbuster shelf's summit — the point where the Black cultural imagination, at industrial scale, became the industry's center of gravity for a season.

description: Robert Barisford Brown Sr. (born February 5, 1969, in Boston, Massachusetts) is an American singer, songwriter, rapper and dancer who grew up in Roxbury's Orchard Park Projects. His debut King of Stage (1986) yielded the No. 1 R&B single “Girlfriend.” His second album, Don't Be Cruel (1988), made him a pioneer of new jack swing alongside Teddy Riley, spawning five Billboard Hot 100 top-ten singles including the No. 1 “My Prerogative” and the Grammy-winning “Every Little Step.” He contributed “On Our Own” to Ghostbusters II (1989), released the platinum album Bobby (1992), and reunited with New Edition for the No. 1 album Home Again (1996). Brown married Whitney Houston in 1992; they divorced in 2007. He continues to perform with New Edition.

name: Babyface
aliases: Kenneth Edmonds; Kenneth Brian Edmonds; Kenny Edmonds
description: Kenneth Brian Edmonds, born in Indianapolis on April 10, 1959, learned songwriting as a shy teenager, took the stage name Babyface in Bootsy Collins's orbit, and served his apprenticeship in the bands Manchild and the Deele, where his partnership with Antonio 'L.A.' Reid began. As a writer-producer team, Edmonds and Reid helped define late-1980s and 1990s R&B, and in 1989 they founded LaFace Records, the Atlanta label that launched Toni Braxton, TLC, Usher, Outkast, and Pink. Babyface's own solo career ran in parallel — Tender Lover and For the Cool in You among his platinum albums — but his deepest imprint is the catalog he wrote and produced for others: Boyz II Men's 'End of the Road' and 'I'll Make Love to You,' Madonna's 'Take a Bow,' Whitney Houston's 'Exhale (Shoop Shoop),' and Mary J. Blige's 'Not Gon' Cry,' which he wrote and produced for the Waiting to Exhale soundtrack, a project he effectively authored end to end. Industry counts credit him with twenty-six number-one R&B hits and thirteen Grammy Awards, including an unmatched run of Producer of the Year honors in the mid-1990s, and with more than 125 Top 10 hits as writer or producer. His quiet, melody-first craft made him the era's trusted balladeer — the man other stars called when a song had to last.

description: Bruno Mars, born Peter Gene Hernandez on October 8, 1985, in Honolulu, Hawaii, is an American singer, songwriter, and producer whose artistry is rooted openly in Black American musical traditions. In 2021 he formed Silk Sonic with Anderson .Paak; their retro-soul album An Evening with Silk Sonic won wide acclaim, and its lead single, "Leave the Door Open," won Record and Song of the Year at the 2022 Grammys. Mars names his debts plainly and performs them as craft, not costume.

name: Barry Jenkins
description: Barry Jenkins (Barry Lamar Jenkins, born November 19, 1979, Miami) is the filmmaker whose Moonlight (2016) won the Academy Award for Best Picture and reset what American independent cinema could be. Raised in Miami's Liberty City and trained at Florida State University's film school (BFA 2003), he made his debut feature, Medicine for Melancholy (2008), for roughly $15,000. Moonlight, made for about $1.5 million, won Best Picture; Jenkins and Tarell Alvin McCraney won Best Adapted Screenplay, and Jenkins was the fourth Black person nominated for Best Director and the second Black director of a Best Picture winner. If Beale Street Could Talk (2018) followed, winning Regina King the Best Supporting Actress Oscar, and his Amazon limited series The Underground Railroad (2021) drew an Emmy directing nomination and a Peabody Award. Early in his career Jenkins worked as a director's assistant on Harpo's television adaptation of Their Eyes Were Watching God (2005) — a formative credit shared, across this very packet, with Zora Neale Hurston (CTL-E-5957).

name: Boyz n the Hood
description: Boyz n the Hood, John Singleton's feature directorial debut, written by Singleton and released by Columbia Pictures in 1991 after a Los Angeles premiere that July 2, follows Tre Styles, sent to live with his father in South Central Los Angeles, in a coming-of-age story built from Singleton's own neighborhood knowledge and drawn from the script he had written as a student — one he insisted on directing himself as a condition of its sale. The industry record followed: at twenty-four, Singleton became the youngest person ever nominated for the Academy Award for Best Director, and the first African American so nominated, with a second nomination for his original screenplay. The film held the first or breakout roles of Ice Cube, Cuba Gooding Jr., Morris Chestnut, and Nia Long, and grossed $57.5 million in North America. It is held in the National Film Registry. The graph files it as the hood-film era's founding text and its moral center — the work that set the terms every successor, including Singleton's own Snowfall (CTL-E-5463) a generation later, had to answer.

description: Busta Rhymes is an American rapper born Trevor Smith Jr. on May 20, 1972, in East Flatbush, Brooklyn, New York, of Jamaican heritage. He moved to Long Island in 1983 and at Uniondale High School met Charlie Brown, Dinco D., and Cut Monitor Milo; the four formed Leaders of the New School and signed with Elektra Records while he was seventeen. The group released A Future Without a Past... in 1991 and T.I.M.E. in 1993 before breaking up in 1994. Rhymes then built a guest-appearance career, including his verse on A Tribe Called Quest's "Scenario," before his solo debut album, The Coming, in 1996; its single "Woo-Hah!! Got You All in Check" reached the Top Ten. His second album, When Disaster Strikes, debuted at number three in 1997, and his seventh studio album, The Big Bang, debuted at number one in 2006. AllMusic also lists him as a member of Flipmode Squad, the crew he fronted. He released Extinction Level Event 2: The Wrath of God in October 2020, Blockbusta in November 2023, and the Dragon Season... The Awakening EP in January 2025, and he has also worked as a producer and taken film and television roles.
